correctness.rationale: For each n>=2 and 0<=k<=n, dominating subsets are exactly the two full layers or the mixed-layer subsets. In a mixed-layer subset, every selected top/bottom vertex sees its respective layer omission count, plus one if its matched opposite partner is absent; this proves both required and sufficient capacity inequalities, with the distinct whole-layer k>=1 boundary. Unique labelling of columns into c,x,y,d yields a multinomial coefficient for each pattern and an exact cardinality exponent. The lower bound |D|>=2(n-k) for mixed-layer sets, with equality only for c=k, x=y=0,d=n-k, combined with the two pure-layer sets establishes the piecewise multiplicities. For k=0 connectedness forces D=V; for k=n the graph has n^2 two-vertex mixed dominators and two extra pure layers only at n=2. A separate graph-neighborhood exhaustive program for all 42 n,k pairs (n=2..8) checked all polynomial coefficients and the minimum multiplicity; selected analytic comparisons covered n=9..35. These experiments support but do not replace the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The recent study of k-limited domination in Cartesian products motivates a complete enumeration beyond just the minimum number. The two-row rook family has unbounded order and degree yet admits a closed all-size multivariate-state classification in a polynomial number of occupancy patterns. The exact polynomial and the sharp binomial-versus-two multiplicity transition resolve the distribution of every feasible size; such counts are mathematically distinct from and not implied by the previously recorded numerical minimization result. Trivial k=0,n cases are integrated only as boundary checks, not advertised as substantive standalone discoveries.
